prompt: The client is valuing an acquisition target. Which takeaway matters most?

options.text: Revenue growth was 72% in three years
options.feedback: True, but margins fell faster, so the target earns less than before.

options.text: EBITDA grew, since revenue rose faster than margins fell
options.feedback: Revenue rose 72%, but the margin fell from 20% to 8%: EBITDA went from $10.0M to $6.9M.

options.text: EBITDA shrank from $10M to $7M despite growth
options.feedback: Right. EBITDA fell from $10.0M (50 × 20%) to $6.9M (86 × 8%) despite revenue growing 72%.

options.text: The target is cutting prices to grow
options.feedback: The chart shows revenue and margin, not prices. That may be true, but nothing here supports it.

explanation: EBITDA fell from $10.0M (50 × 20%) to $6.9M (86 × 8%) despite revenue growing 72%.

extras.proof: EBITDA fell from $10.0M (50 × 20%) to $6.9M (86 × 8%) despite revenue growing 72%.
